title: Super helpful for staying on task
body: I have certain tasks (such as cleaning, or managing 20+ work queues) where it’s important not to either over-invest and run out of time or under-invest and let things get out of hand. I love this app, because it takes all of the guesswork out of this. I just hit start and go from one step to the next, and it has the right audio prompts to let me know when I need to wrap up a step and move onto the next thing or not. I’ve been a subscriber for several years now. In terms of improvements, the only thing on my wishlist is that I wish we could have more options for music tracks, so we could apply different music to different routines. There’s only one track right now. I think it would be nice to have 5 or more good options.

title: FORGET ANY OTHER APP
body:
Other apps have too much going on and are way too distracting for ADHD me. 
THIS APP THOUGH, the routine is TIMED, isn’t tied to a specific hour (even been like, “oh no, it’s 8:01 so I’ll just have to wait ‘til 8:30!”?)- but has set reminders, recommends a TRIGGER to start the routine, and is overall simply and EASY.

Listen, I’ve tried EVERY SINGLE ROUTINE/SCHEDULE/HABIT app/planner/calendar out there. Seriously. It burns out after a while THIS ONE WORKS FOR ME.

My ONLY suggestion is if there was a widget option- shows me when my routine’s coming up, and an immediate button for me to start the timed routine from the widget. When it’s not in my face, I can forget or accidentally swipe my notifs.

It’s only $26 bucks. I paid for $5 to try for the month and it’s already a godsend. This plus a goal streaks app together, boom.

*mic drop*

title: Life changing!
body:
It’s been 4 days since I started using RoutineFlow and I love it!

I was recommended this app by my psychologist when discussing my ADHD symptoms. One of my main challenge was I was waking up late every day and rushing to the shower to get ready and enter my remote work meeting 5 minutes late. Every morning felt chaotic and repeating the same thing everyday was demoralising. 

Once I started RoutineFlow, I started waking up an hour early, finding time to have breakfast, shower peacefully and attend my work meeting on time. I’m also more organised now. For example, I now made a routine that I start at the end of my workday to tidy up my desk and pick out clothes for the next day. 

I think what really works for me in this app is the audio and visual reminders. Once I start a routine, I can see how much time has passed and how much time is left in the form of a large progress bar (this is useful because I can see the progress bar when without my glasses when taking a shower). The app also gives audio reminders when a step is halfway done and when there is 30 seconds remaining. 

My wish from the developer is to allow me to configure the audio reminder so that I can set it to a pre configured value, because I feel 30 seconds is too little time. The other thing is that the voice is the old robotic voice which sounds very unnatural. It would be really nice if it had a more realistic voice or even the voice from Siri. 

Finally, the daily streaks and insights view adds a level of gamification that really seems to help me. I’m obsessed with creating new routines and tracking them in the app!

title: Love it with a few caveats
body:
I really like this app for the most part, and I haven’t found another one that doesn’t jump to the next task automatically. You must check off that the task is done before it starts the timer for the next task, which is great because if you get behind on the apps that automate the task jumping, all of a sudden you’re 3 tasks behind and the routine becomes useless. This also gives you the anticipated time of completion, which is a helpful and rare feature. However, there are a few things that bug me. When I’m trying to rearrange tasks, the app doesn’t scroll up as I’m dragging, so I have to drop the task, scroll down, and then move it again, which is annoying since I have long routines with lots of tasks. 

I also wish there was an option to see all the steps at once while I’m in routine mode (sort of like on google maps where you can check the route overview without stopping the directions). If I run over on one task and realize I’m going to be late, I’d like to quickly check which tasks are coming up and decide which ones I can skip or adjust without stopping the timer. 

The "do later" feature is useful, but it seems to move the task to the end of the list permanently, which I don’t want. I’d prefer it to just temporarily move the task.

Lastly, I don’t think there needs to be a save button. Changes should save automatically, and having to hit "save" just adds an unnecessary step with no benefit. If I make a change, it should be saved right away so I don’t risk losing the input.
